notes: §14.6.10 1) leaves the result of overlapping, differently described operands undefined (Annex A.2 item 36; §4.4 2) makes the run unit conforming), so every behavior conforms and the goldens pin WiseOwl COBOL's DOCUMENTED choice, CONFORMANCE.md §3 D-OVL1/D-OVL2 (owner decision 2026-10-01, kb/Work PB1907, PB1910): a MOVE or ADD reads its sender in full before writing the receiver (snapshot), except the families where GnuCOBOL 3.2.0's libcob writes or prepares the receiver while it reads the sender, which WiseOwl COBOL follows (measured with a built cobc, ASCII and -fsign=EBCDIC): a JUSTIFIED RIGHT receiver's leading pad positions are space-filled before a shorter alphanumeric sender is read (JUST=[A A ]), and a numeric DISPLAY or PACKED-DECIMAL receiver is converted IN PLACE from a numeric DISPLAY, alphanumeric or (DISPLAY receiver) PACKED-DECIMAL sender, the receiver cleared and written digit by digit from the sender's bytes as the storage then holds them (NUM-MOVE=[0000], PK-TAIL=23300, SMEAR-N=3333, P-SIGN=+4567), both only where the overlap is a compile-time fact (StorageExtent). Numeric-edited receivers, PACKED-DECIMAL into PACKED-DECIMAL, and a signed DISPLAY sender into a BINARY receiver under the IBM convention keep the snapshot (D-OVL2). retired-witness: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/CodeGen/Verbs/MoveEmitter.cs#EmitOverlapPrefill (the method was renamed EmitOverlapStore when the overlap treatment grew from a receiver prefill to the library's in-place conversions (kb/Work PB1910); EmitOverlapStore and EmitInPlaceStore are the same rule's renderings)
